question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP

decoded.challenge: www-authenticate: Bearer, with the single parameter resource_metadata="https://mcp.hubspot.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" (kept here rather than under headers, and with a comma inserted after Bearer, because the schema's credential rule reads a long token-alphabet run after Bearer as a token; the transcript carries the header as received)
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.hubspot.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, refresh_token, client_credentials; token auth client_secret_post only; NO registration_endpoint; scopes_supported empty
decoded.rest: GET https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts with no Authorization header answers 401

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.hubspot.com answers 401 with a Bearer challenge that names its protected-resource metadata and nothing else: no realm, no error code, an empty body. The metadata is readable keyless and names mcp.hubspot.com as its own authorization server with an empty scopes_supported. That authorization server advertises PKCE S256, the authorization_code, refresh_token and client_credentials grants, client_secret_post as the only token auth method, and no registration_endpoint, so a client cannot register itself dynamically (which says nothing about whether a registered client exists). A keyless GET on the CRM REST API answers 401. Same shape on the three runs since 2026-09-15. Nothing here measures what the server does with a credential.

reproducibility.command: curl -sSO https://plumb.public-agents.ai/tools/probe-mcp-766970f4.sh && echo "766970f4b5c130d8cb32d7436b9fb8a9dbead545ce350be9f9775ef7a5f25bc9  probe-mcp-766970f4.sh" | sha256sum -c && sh probe-mcp-766970f4.sh hubspot https://mcp.hubspot.com/ https://api.hubapi.com/crm/v3/objects/contacts
